findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:408-427 (out-dir reuse deletes receipt.json before capture) vs README.md:67 ('later checks enforce the union of everything ever required, so a matrix can be widened but never quietly narrowed'), README.md:235, SKILL.md:71-73
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: after `check --require 'desktop:*,mobile:*'` had stored required_coverage on a full run, I re-ran capture into the SAME --out-dir with `--tabs Overview --viewports desktop=1280x800 --screenshot-mode viewport` against the defect page (docs/demo). The cleanup removed receipt.json, so the new receipt had no required_coverage and no inspections; one attestation later a plain `check` printed 'OK: every screenshot inspected against its current bytes, nothing failed', exit 0, with the clipped mobile view never captured. The same path erases a `fail` attestation ('a fail is final for that run'). Out-dir reuse is explicitly supported (README:69, SKILL.md:55), so the 'stored requirement' is only as sticky as the file capture is told to delete; an agent that reuses the directory the task named gets a green gate without ever passing --require again.
findings.amendment: When reusing an out-dir whose prior receipt.json parses as this tool's receipt, carry `required_coverage` (and a `supersedes_run_id`) forward into the new receipt before writing it; alternatively refuse reuse when the prior receipt has required_coverage or any `fail` inspection unless `--replace` is given. Update README:67/235 to say the requirement is bound to the receipt and survives out-dir reuse (or that reuse is refused).
findings.mechanical_test: In tests/test_capture.sh: capture tabs.html with `--tabs 'Overview,Details' --viewports 'a=800x600,b=390x844'` into $d; attest all; `run 0 check $d/receipt.json --require 'a:*,b:*'`; re-capture into the same $d with `--tabs Overview --viewports a=800x600 --screenshot-mode viewport --no-aria-snapshot`; attest its one PNG; `run 3 check $d/receipt.json` and `grep -q 'MISSING COVERAGE: b:\*' stderr` (or `run 64` on the re-capture if refusal is chosen). npm test passes.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:344-354 (wildcard matches 'at least one captured shot') vs README.md:64,196,242 and docs/example/run-2/receipt.json required_coverage ['desktop:*','mobile:*'], SKILL.md:68 ('mobile:*')
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: against the fixed demo page I captured with `--tabs Overview` only (Orders tab dropped), both viewports, attested the two PNGs, and `check --require 'desktop:*,mobile:*'` — the exact form the README recommends and the committed example stores — exited 0 with 'OK'. `--require 'desktop:Orders,mobile:Orders'` correctly reported MISSING COVERAGE. A `*` on the state side is satisfied by any single state, so the documented invocation lets an agent silently drop every tab but one; README:220 ('Capturing less does not help either') demonstrates only viewport narrowing. Readers will copy the wildcard form and believe the tab matrix is enforced.
findings.amendment: Document that `*` means 'at least one captured value' and cannot detect a dropped tab; change the README/SKILL examples and the committed run-2 requirement to explicit pairs (`desktop:Overview,desktop:Orders,mobile:Overview,mobile:Orders`), and have SKILL.md instruct agents to list every state by name. Optionally expand `V:*` against the union of states named elsewhere in required_coverage.
findings.mechanical_test: Add to test 17: capture tabs.html with `--tabs Overview --viewports 'desk=800x600,mob=390x844' --screenshot-mode viewport --no-aria-snapshot`; attest both; `run 0 check ... --require 'desk:*,mob:*'` documents the wildcard limit, then `run 3 check ... --require 'desk:Details'` with `grep -q 'MISSING COVERAGE: desk:Details'`. `grep -n 'mobile:\*' README.md SKILL.md` returns only lines that also state the wildcard limitation.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:281-282 (attest matches `basename(entry.path) === wanted` regardless of directory) and 286 (digest read from the receipt's own artifact, not from the file named by --path)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: I placed a 9-byte non-PNG at <elsewhere>/mobile--overview--full.png and ran `attest run-2b/receipt.json --path <elsewhere>/mobile--overview--full.png`; it was accepted ('attested: mobile--overview--full.png (pass)') because the digest was taken from run-2b's own file. Concretely, an inspector who opens run-3's `mobile--overview--full.png` (same basename, different bytes) and attests run-2's receipt with that absolute path records a pass against evidence they never viewed. The receipt's 'bound to the PNG's sha256' guarantee then binds to bytes the inspector did not look at.
findings.amendment: When --path contains a directory component, resolve it and require it to be the receipt's artifact (same resolved path) or, if it is a different existing file, hash that file and refuse unless its sha256 equals the receipt entry's; otherwise error 'path names a different file than the receipt's artifact'.

findings.location: package-lock.json:3 and :9 ("version": "0.1.0") vs package.json:3 ("version": "0.2.0"), SKILL.md:8, CHANGELOG.md
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: the lockfile committed for the 0.2.0 release still records the root package as 0.1.0 (CHANGELOG says the lock was regenerated for Node 20; the version was not bumped). `npm ci` tolerates it, but the first `npm install` by any contributor rewrites the lock and dirties the tree, and the mismatch is visible on the GitHub 'dependencies' view of a repo whose whole pitch is checkable claims.
findings.amendment: Run `npm install --package-lock-only` and commit the lock with version 0.2.0.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:230-268 (withReceiptLock/writeReceiptAtomic) and 323-332 (check's coverage write), dispatch at 392-398 rethrows non-UsageError
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: with the run directory chmod 555, both `attest` and `check --require <new pair>` crash with a raw Node stack trace ('node:fs:560 return binding.open', 7 stack lines) and exit 1 — the code reserved for 'capture failed'. `check` on a read-only receipt (a CI artifact, a committed example) therefore cannot even report gate status once a new requirement is passed, and README:283's 'usage errors exiting 64 without stack traces' does not cover the most likely filesystem error.
findings.amendment: Catch EACCES/EROFS/EPERM in withReceiptLock and writeReceiptAtomic and rethrow as UsageError('cannot write receipt <path>: <code>'); for `check`, when the write fails, still print the gate report and exit with the gate code plus a 'REQUIREMENT NOT STORED' line.
findings.mechanical_test: `cp -r $t/req $t/ro; chmod 555 $t/ro; run 64 attest $t/ro/receipt.json --path desk--overview--viewport.png --verdict pass --note 'read-only directory test' --by tester; ! grep -q '    at ' $t/stderr; chmod 755 $t/ro`. npm test passes.

findings.location: scripts/capture.mjs:413-422 (priorReceipt = any JSON with numeric schema_version; then pattern-based deletion) vs README.md:274 ('pointing the collector at an assets folder cannot delete anything')
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: an out-dir containing `receipt.json` = `{"schema_version":1}` (not this tool's receipt) plus a foreign `brand--logo--full.png` was accepted for reuse and the foreign PNG was deleted; only `notes.txt` survived. Any directory that holds some other tool's receipt.json with a numeric schema_version unlocks deletion of every `*--*--{viewport,full}.png` / `*--*.aria.yml` in it. The README's absolute claim is therefore slightly over-stated.
findings.amendment: Require the prior receipt to validate via readReceipt (schema 3/4, run_id string, screenshots array) and delete only receipt.json plus the files named in that receipt's screenshots[] (basename, within the directory), not pattern matches.

findings.location: README.md:270 ('the first survives only when it is a plain route word') vs scripts/capture.mjs:193 (`/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]{0,31}$/`)
findings.failure_mode: OBSERVED: console text `https://intra.corp.example/karina/private-notes/2026?tok=1` became `https://intra.corp.example/karina/[REDACTED]/[REDACTED]?REDACTED`, and a failed request to `/karina-qian/notes` kept `/karina-qian/[REDACTED]`. A first path segment that is a username or tenant slug (GitHub-style `/user/repo`, `/acme-corp/…`) survives because the regex only tests for letters and hyphens; the README wording implies a route-word vocabulary. Also OBSERVED: a bare email address in console text ('user jane.doe@corp.example') is kept; the README does not claim emails are removed, but the sentence 'identifiers in URL path segments never reaching the receipt' (README:283) is broader than what holds.
findings.amendment: Reword README:270/283 to 'the first segment survives when it consists only of letters and hyphens (which can include a user or tenant name)', or tighten the rule to redact every segment unless --keep-paths.
findings.mechanical_test: Fixture logging `https://h.example/karina-qian/x`; capture; `grep -q 'h.example/\[REDACTED\]' receipt.json` (if tightened) or README diff contains 'letters and hyphens'.

The receipt records `config.user_agent` verbatim (OBSERVED: AGENT_VERIFICATION_USER_AGENT='MyLab/1.0 (someone@example.invalid)' landed in receipt.json). If your own shell exports a lab-wide User-Agent to satisfy a per-request policy, every receipt you share will carry it. Is that acceptable, or should the receipt store only a sha256/boolean for the override?

README:13 says the collector 'was written by one model and audited by others'; docs/reviews/README.md discloses both prior reviewers are Claude-family, and this review is too, while SKILL.md:20 asks for a different model family. For 0.2.0 the code was implemented by Codex, so the cross-family claim holds for this release's code but not for the 0.1.x reviews of Claude-written code. Do you want README:13 to say exactly that, so the claim survives a sceptical reader?

Out-dir reuse currently discards a `fail` attestation and stored coverage with the receipt (finding 1). Is 'a fail is final for that run' meant to be enforceable across a re-capture into the same directory, or is a fresh run_id by definition a clean slate? Your answer decides between carry-forward and refusal.

Do you want a wildcard in --require to keep its current 'at least one' meaning (finding 2), or to expand against the tabs named in the original capture command so `desktop:*` means every state the task listed? The former is simpler and needs only a doc change; the latter needs a place to record the intended tab list independent of what a narrowed capture wrote.

The walkthrough and the fixed demo were captured with system Chrome (`chrome: null` recorded, Playwright-bundled Chromium not used per browserPath preference); the README does not say which browser produced the committed PNGs. Fine for 0.2.0, or do you want the receipt to record the resolved executable/version so digests are reproducible across machines?

The commit link in README:203 uses `../../commit/c78fd09`, which resolves only on github.com. Are you committed to GitHub as the sole rendering surface for this README (agentskills.io listing, npm, mirrors would show a broken link)?
